import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 400

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/400](https://www.erdosproblems.com/400)
-/

open Nat Filter Finset
open scoped Asymptotics Topology

namespace Erdos400

/--
For any $k\geq 2$ let $g_k(n)$ denote the maximum value of $(a_1+\cdots+a_k)-n$
where $a_1,\ldots,a_k$ are integers such that $a_1!\cdots a_k! \mid n!$.
-/
noncomputable def g (k n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup { ((∑ i, a i) - n) | (a : Fin k → ℕ) (_ : (∏ i, (a i) !) ∣ n !) }

/--
Can one show that $\sum_{n\leq x}g_k(n) \sim c_k x\log x$ for some constant $c_k$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_400.parts.i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (k ≥ 2), ∃ c : ℝ,
      (fun x : ℕ ↦ (∑ n ∈ Icc 1 x, (g k n : ℝ))) ~[atTop]
      (fun x : ℕ ↦ c * x * Real.log x) := by
  sorry

/--
Is it true that there is a constant $c_k$ such that for almost all $n < x$ we have
$g_k(n)=c_k\log x+o(\log x)$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_400.parts.ii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (k ≥ 2), ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ ε > 0,
      Tendsto (fun x : ℕ ↦
        (((Icc 1 x).filter (fun n ↦
          |(g k n : ℝ) - c * Real.log x| ≤ ε * Real.log x)).card : ℝ) / x)
        atTop (𝓝 1) := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős and Graham write that it is easy to show that $g_k(n) \ll_k \log n$ always, but the best
possible constant is unknown.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_400.variants.upper_bound (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≥ 2) :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (g k n : ℝ)) ≪ (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log (n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry


/-- For $k \ge 2$, $g_k(n) > 0$. We show this by choosing $a = (n, 1, 0, \ldots, 0)$. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_400.variants.g_pos (k n : ℕ) (h: k ≥ 2) : 0 < g k n := by
  obtain ⟨k', rfl⟩ : ∃ k', k = k' + 2 := ⟨k - 2, by omega⟩
  simp only [g]
  -- Witness: a(0) = n, a(1) = 1, a(i) = 0 for i ≥ 2
  set a : Fin (k' + 2) → ℕ := fun i =>
    if (i : ℕ) = 0 then n else if (i : ℕ) = 1 then 1 else 0 with ha_def
  have h_prod : ∏ i : Fin (k' + 2), (a i)! = n ! := by
    rw [Fin.prod_univ_succ]; simp [ha_def]
    rw [Fin.prod_univ_succ]; simp
  have h_sum : ∑ i : Fin (k' + 2), a i = n + 1 := by
    rw [Fin.sum_univ_succ]; simp [ha_def]
  -- 1 is in the set
  have hmem : 1 ∈ {(∑ i, b i) - n | (b : Fin (k' + 2) → ℕ) (_ : ∏ i, (b i)! ∣ n !)} :=
    ⟨a, h_prod ▸ dvd_refl n !, by omega⟩
  -- The set is bounded above by (k'+2) * n!
  have hbdd : BddAbove {(∑ i, b i) - n | (b : Fin (k' + 2) → ℕ) (_ : ∏ i, (b i)! ∣ n !)} := by
    refine ⟨(k' + 2) * n !, ?_⟩
    rintro x ⟨b, hb, rfl⟩
    calc (∑ i, b i) - n
        ≤ ∑ i, b i := Nat.sub_le _ _
      _ ≤ ∑ i : Fin (k' + 2), (b i)! :=
          Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => Nat.self_le_factorial _
      _ ≤ Finset.univ.card • n ! := by
          apply Finset.sum_le_card_nsmul; intro i _
          exact le_trans (Finset.single_le_prod' (fun j _ =>
            Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.mpr (Nat.factorial_ne_zero _))
            (Finset.mem_univ i)) (Nat.le_of_dvd (Nat.factorial_pos n) hb)
      _ = (k' + 2) * n ! := by simp [smul_eq_mul]
  exact Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.one_pos (le_csSup hbdd hmem)

end Erdos400

reformulations.difference: Lean uses a natural-number supremum of truncated differences and permits zero factorial arguments, rather than directly taking the maximum of the signed integer expression. The recent paper explicitly requires positive arguments.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For fixed k,n every admissible coordinate satisfies a_i ≤ max n 1, and admissible tuples exist, so the supremum is an attained maximum with no unbounded-set default involved. For k ≥ 2 a positive excess is attainable, so truncating negative candidate values to zero cannot change the maximum. Replacing each zero coordinate by 1 preserves its factorial and increases the sum, so restricting to positive arguments also leaves the maximum unchanged. In /workspace/review/g_tests.lean, signed_max_iff and positive_signed_max_iff prove the corresponding maximum characterizations without sorry.

reformulations.difference: The source asks for g_k(n) = c_k log x + o(log x) for almost all n < x. Lean instead requires, for every ε > 0, that the proportion satisfying |g_k(n) − c_k log x| ≤ ε log x in 1 ≤ n ≤ x tend to 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each ε, the Lean condition is exactly that the complementary exceptional count is o(x). Conversely, from these conditions for ε = 1/j, choose increasing thresholds X_j beyond which the exceptional proportion is at most 1/j. A diagonal choice j = j(x) tending to infinity gives both an o(x) exceptional set and an o(log x) uniform error outside it. The reverse implication follows immediately from these two little-o bounds. Including n = x changes the count by at most one, hence the proportion by at most 1/x. The complementary-count equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/asymptotic_tests.lean; the diagonal and endpoint arguments were checked mathematically, not fully formalized.

review.notes: All five declarations were checked. Additional Lean tests establish g k 0 = k and g k 1 = k − 1, prove a finite enumerator equal to g, and compute small cases for k = 0,1,2,3. Part (i) forces c > 0; this was proved without sorry, so the unrestricted real existential introduces no zero-constant loophole. The custom ≪ notation is Big-O atTop, with constants allowed to depend on k. The proved g_pos lemma has no sorryAx dependency. Direct requests to the live source encountered Cloudflare; the August 2026 archive, currently fetched source-linked database, and latest Li preprint provide no evidence of a status discrepancy. The preprint supplies partial bounds, not the requested asymptotic constant. The reviewed file still matches the specified commit exactly; review experiments were confined to /workspace/review/.
